rows.author: A024
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING THAT A SUBJECT ON ILLEGAL DRUGS BE INCORPORATED IN THE SCHOOL CURRICULA IN ALL PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SCHOOLS
rows.abstract: Rationale: Making our youth aware of the consequences of illegal drugs in one's life will minimize drug abuse and the incidence of drug-related crimes.  With the enactment of this bill, the young generation could be made aware that many homes and precious lives have been destroyed becuase of the proliferation of drug addiction in the country. It is through education that our government will be able to solve the drug problem in our country.  In view thereof, approval of this bill is highly recommended. Mandates the following --- "SECTION 1. A subject on illegal drugs, its effects on the person and society, shall be incorporated in the school curricula in all public and private, elementary, secondary and tertiary schools.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 1997-02-03

rows.author: B002
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING A FIVE-YEAR MORATORIUM ON THE INCREASE IN RENTALS OF ALL RESIDENTIAL UNITS
rows.abstract: Rationale: Rentals of residential units is an added financial burden to families. Some have to tighten their belts a little more to be able to cope with the higher rate of rental of residential units and the spiraling cost of basic commodities. Withthe existing average of Six Thousand Pesos (P6,000.00) monthly rental of residential units, families with only a member thereof as the sole breadwinner would likely resort to squatting just to cope with the high cost of today's basic human needs. Mandates the following --- "SECTION 1. A five-year moratorium is hereby declared on the increase in rentals of all residential units with monthly rental of Ten Thousand Pesos (P10,000.00) and below." "SECTION 2. This Act shall take effect on January 1,, 1998 following its publication in at least two (2) newspaperss of general circulation.
rows.status: Substituted by HB09092

rows.author: A037
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 277(C) OF THE LABOR CODE, AS AMENDED, BY REQUIRING AN EMPLOYER TO FURNISH HIS EMPLOYEE WITH A WRITTEN CONTRACT OF EMPLOYMENT
rows.abstract: Rationale: One of the reasons why dockets of Labor Tribunals continue to be clogged with cases involving the issue of employer-employ ee relationships is the failure of employers to provide their employees with a written contract of employment. It is disheartening to note that almost 80% of our work force does not possess a written contract of employment, thus, employees are usually bereft of any evidence proving that they are actual employees of a certain company. > Declares that IT SHALL BE THE DUTY OF AN EMPLOYER TO FURNISH HIS EMPLOYEE WITH A WRITTEN CONTRACT OF EMPLOYMENT. THE WRITTEN CONTRACT OF EMPLOYMENT SHALL SERVE AS PRIMA FACIE PRESUMPTION OF THE EXISTENCE OF AN EMPLOYER-EMPLOY EE RELATIONSHIP.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 1997-02-03

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING LOCAL OFFICIALS FROM CLAIMING TRAVEL EXPENSES AND ALLOWANCES WHEN ATTENDING COURT HEARINGS OR LITIGATION RELATED ACTIVITIES OUTSIDE OF HIS JURISDICTION EXCEPT WHEN REPRESENTING THE PROVINCE, CITY OR MUNICIPALITY IN HIS CAPACITY ASTHE LOCAL CHIEF EXECUTIVE, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Declares it UNLAWFUL  for the following local officials to CLAIM travel expenses and/or allowances when attending court hearings or litigation - related activities outside of his jurisdiction, EXCEPT when representing the province, city or municipality: (1) Provincial Governor; (2) Municipal and (3) city mayors. Penalizes the official found guilty of violating this Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 1997-02-03

rows.title_full: AN ACT SUBJECTING THE INTELLIGENCE FUND OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS TO AN AUDIT BY THE COMMISSION ON AUDIT
rows.abstract: Rationale: While the Provincial Governors, City and Municipal Mayors enjoy the luxury and the special privilege of spending government funds or the so called "Intelligence Fund" at will without the necessity of subjecting it to COA Audit, it is alsolamentable that the use of such fund has been abused to the detriment of the taxpayer. It has come to a point where these officials used the money to advance their political edge over their opponent, thereby making the political playing field uneven. Mandates  this provision --- "SECTION 1. Disbursements of Intelligence Funds by Local Government Units shall be made only in accordance with existing budgeting, accounting and auditing rules and regulations."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 1997-02-03

rows.title_full: AN ACT ABOLISHING THE PRESIDENTIAL COMMISSION ON GOOD GOVERNMENT (PCGG) AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Former President Corazon c. Aquino, through Executive Order No. 1, created the Presidential Commission on Good Government (PCGG) is tasked to recover ill-gotten wealth accumulated by some of our public officials and to return the same toits rightful owners - the filipino people.  With this mandate, PCGG was granted legal immunity. Agents of PCGG could not be asked to testify or required to produce evidence in any judicial, legislative or administrative proceedings concerning its official actions. > Despite this awesome mandate, the performance record of the PCGG leaves much to be desired.  Many of its commissioners or agents were involved in graft and corruption and many of its cases in courts are dismissed or lost because of ppoor investigation and documentation. <Requires the devolution of the PCGG powers and functions of investigation and prosecution upon the Office of the Department of Justice (DOJ).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 1997-02-03

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO POSTPONE THE MAY 12, 1997 BARANGAY ELECTIONS AND RESET TO THE SECOND MONDAY OF MAY 1998, TO COINCIDE WITH THE NATIONAL AND LOCAL ELECTIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: While there is a legal basis for the holding of the electoral exercise on May 12 this year, there are however compelling reasons justifying its resetting to coincide with the national and local election in May 1998.> The national and local elections in May 1998 are only a year away from May 1997.  The five-year gap will mean a saving for the government of some P900 million, which can be better used to alleviate poverty, support livelihood projects, enhance health and social servicesand construct infrastructures .

rows.title_full: AN ACT WHICH SEEKS TO PRIORITIZE INVESTMENTS IN PRIMARY EDUCATION OVER THE SECONDARY AND TERTIARY EDUCATION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Primary Education Priority Investment Act of 1996" Aims to shift government spending from secondary and tertiary edcuation TO PRIMARY EDUCATION. States the INVESTMENT PRIORITY for this purpose as follows: (a) Funds for secondary and tertiary education shall be limited to the maintenance of existing facilities with no new construction being authorized until succh time that the provisions of paragraph (b) hereof shall have been complied with; and (b) Funds remaining shall be used for primary education, particularly, in the construction andd maintenance of school buildings and facilities, provision of equipments and improvement of teaching, instructional materials and curriculum especially in areas where such are inadequate and until such tiime as the need for such for all localities nationwide shall have been met.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING THAT THE PROVINCIAL, CITY OR MUNICIPAL ASSESSOR SHALL UNDERTAKE A GENERAL REVISION OF REAL PROPERTY ASSESSMENT EVERY FIVE (5) YEARS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Rationale: The Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160) regulates the revision of assessment and classification of real properties. Under Sec. 219 and Sec. 220 of RA 7160, assessment is undertaken every three (3) years. This means, a higher real estate tax after each assessment. If correlated with the rising percentage of inflation, it spells and unncessary burden affecting the majority of our people. > Provides, therefore for the following --- "SEC. 219. General Revision of Assessments and Property Classification. - The provincial, city or municipal assessor shall undertake a general revision of real property assessments within two (2) years after the effectivity of this Code and every [three (3)] FIVE (5) years thereafter."

rows.abstract: Rationale: The outright shiftly of resources from secondary and tertiary TO PRIMARY EDUCATION  may lead to waste and student dislocation. Resources may be redisplayed to ...
